faq.q: Who is exempt from paying advance tax?
faq.a: Resident senior citizens (aged 60 years or more) who do not have any income from business or profession are exempt from paying advance tax. Also, individuals whose total tax liability after TDS is less than ₹10,000 are not required to pay advance tax.

faq.q: What happens if I make a capital gain late in the year?
faq.a: If you earn capital gains income after an advance tax installment due date, you can pay the tax on this income in the next remaining installment. If no installment remains, you should pay it before March 31 to avoid interest.

faq.q: How do I calculate my advance tax?
faq.a: You need to estimate your total income from all sources for the entire financial year (April 1 to March 31). Then, calculate the tax on this estimated income as per the current tax slabs. Subtract any TDS that has already been deducted or will be deducted. The remaining amount is your estimated advance tax liability.

faq.q: Can I revise my advance tax estimate?
faq.a: Yes, you can revise your estimate of income and tax liability in subsequent installments. If you initially underestimated, you can pay more in later installments to cover the shortfall and avoid penalties. If you overestimated, you can pay less in later installments.

faq.q: What if December 15th falls on a holiday?
faq.a: If an advance tax due date falls on a Sunday or a public holiday, you can make the payment on the next working day without incurring any penalty.
